tasks.title: Implement persistent actor identity, writer lease, and checked counters
steps: Generate IDs from OS cryptographic randomness through a narrow platform adapter; accept injected generators for collision/error tests. Persist atomically before creating operations; do not derive uniqueness from presence or 16-bit random allocation.

Lock a producer/stream writer across processes. Detect observable duplicate ownership/conflicting actor payloads. Keep private actor state outside shared document stores so ordinary document copying creates a new actor; require an explicit fork-identity operation when copying private device state. Identical disconnected clones cannot always be detected before exchange; document this limit.
Recover next counters from durable own log/checkpoint; reserve IDs without reuse and check increments/range arithmetic before mutation. Widen clocks and affected origin/vector fields consistently.
acceptance: Offline enrollment of separate devices produces independent actors; restart cannot reuse a durable operation ID.

Concurrent local writers, corrupted identity state, random-source failure, observable identity conflicts, and uint64 exhaustion produce typed errors without silent fallback to actor 1. Explicitly forked private state uses fresh identity; normal shared-store copies never copy writer identity.

tasks.title: Adopt persistent actor identity in operations and make values opaque
steps: Write the identity contract first: what a Lamport identity becomes (persistent ActorId plus a checked 64-bit counter, per R1), what total order the engine relies on, and which of those uses are convergence-critical rather than merely identifying. Prove the ordering laws against an independent model before touching the engine.

Complete vnext-identity.md section 3.1 before production adoption: specify operation/item/causal-clock domains, checked durable run-interval reservation or explicit subidentity, split/deletion/undo mapping, and unused-reservation recovery under contiguous coverage. Add independent multi-scalar/split/undo/restart, multi-document/stream, remote-clock, gap, and exhaustion fixtures. A comparator-only model does not authorize mechanically replacing character timestamps with one counter per operation.

Replace the 16-bit replica_id and 32-bit counter in the engine's identity types. The ordering must remain a deterministic total order that every replica computes identically, because origin breaks ties between fragments that share a locator and normalize_fragments exists to handle exactly that case. A locally assigned slot would diverge here and must not be used.

Measure the cost. Every Lamport is embedded in FragmentSummary, which the SumTree aggregates on every edit, so widening the identity widens the hot path. Record bytes-per-identity before and after so the optimization phase inherits a number rather than a surprise.

Make Buffer and IdList take an ActorId and expose it. Keep the legacy integer constructor only if it cannot silently mint an identity that looks valid; an operation carrying a default-constructed (invalid) ActorId is rejected, per P02.
Opaque operation values: move construction and field layout out of the public header so the fast paths that touch fields do so through internal accessors.
acceptance: The independent model and the engine agree on ordering for every generated pair of identities, including equal-locator ties from different actors.
Two distinct ActorIds never share an identity, and a default-constructed ActorId is rejected as invalid_identity rather than treated as actor 0.
The recorded before/after size of an identity is stated in the task log, and no convergence test regresses.

The identity-allocation contract and independent fixtures prove non-aliasing across character runs/splits/deletions/undo and specify reservation/log failure semantics; P06b/P07/L02 inherit those obligations. A checked scalar counter by itself does not satisfy this gate.
tasks.verification: Run the identity model and Buffer/IdList convergence suites in Debug, Release, and ASan; state the measured sizeof(Lamport) and sizeof(FragmentSummary) before and after.
tasks.gate: Ordering and identity-allocation contracts and independent models must exist and run before engine types change; comparator-only evidence leaves allocation/recovery obligations incomplete.
tasks.split_rationale: Split out of P06 on 2026-10-04. P06 asked for opaque values and versioned sparse codecs in one step, but the actor identity is serialized by both the wire codec and the store, so the identity change cannot land before the codecs without either changing those formats outside this task's ownership or introducing a representation the codec task immediately rewrites. The identity work is therefore sequenced first *within* P06 rather than before it, which keeps it a discrete reviewable step without an impossible ordering.

docs/specs/vnext-identity.md sections 3.1-3.8 (2026-10-05) -- the allocation-domain contract the review required: the operation/item/causal domains, run-interval reservation, split/deletion/undo derivation, the causal raise, exhaustion bounds, abandoned reservations becoming explicit gap records, and per-(actor, stream) independence. Section 3.8 states what the model does and does not prove.

libs/collabtext/tests/reference/IdentityAllocationModel.h -- the independent model: its own actor comparison, counter, overflow-safe bound, result vocabulary, run derivation, and contiguous-prefix frontier. It calls no production allocator.

libs/collabtext/tests/tst_identity_allocation_model.cpp -- 16 cases: exhaustion at every boundary in section 3.5, the model-versus-CheckedCounter comparison (fixed table plus 400 seeded randomised runs), non-aliasing across 120 operations, split derivation, deletion identity, undo/redo parity, the full insert/split/delete/undo/redo/restart lifecycle, two documents and two streams, an abandoned reservation becoming a gap, and maximum-counter-is-not-contiguity.

libs/collabtext/include/collabtext/ActorId.h + src/identity/ReplicaState.cpp -- CheckedCounter::reserve_run, the checked all-or-nothing interval reservation the contract needs, tested against the model.

Mutation-checked (allocation gate): removing the run-length bound in production reserve_run fails the two comparison tests; putting the operation identity back on its last item (the legacy aliasing) fails 3 cases; dropping the frontier's contiguity requirement initially passed 16/16, which was a real gap in the fixtures -- a late-joining replica case was added and the mutation is now caught.

docs/specs/vnext-identity.md -- §5 is now MEASURED on the migrated engine, not projected: Identity 24, UndoMapKey 24, FragmentSummary 56 (1.4x of the 40-byte baseline), Fragment 120, Global 40->64, Anchor 12->32. The two rows the original projection omitted are called out with the reason they do not land on the hot path.

libs/collabtext/tests/tst_identity_types.cpp -- 21 cases pinning adoption: the identity is an ActorId plus a uint64 (static_assert on both), the order is total over 128 generated identities, distinct actors never share an identity, a default-constructed actor is the least identity and never valid, counters survive the old 32-bit ceiling, and Global's laws (observe/get/observed/observed_all/join/meet/coverage_intersection, sparse ordering, heap promotion, copies) hold with 128-bit keys. Written before the migration: it did not compile, because Crdt::Identity did not exist.

Bug this suite and the migrated codecs caught together: the deletion-run encoder emitted [[\"actor\",counter],5] with the run's opening bracket dropped, so every edit carrying a deletion run failed to decode. The decoder refusing it is why it surfaced as four test failures rather than as silent data loss.

Wire-boundary invalid-actor rejection: tst_serialization.cpp asserts that a version vector whose key is the all-zero actor hex does not decode. There is no actor 0, and silently dropping the component would understate the coverage a watermark is computed from.

Schema 3 -> 4 in SidecarManifest, documented as a clean cut: the identity encoding (16-bit replica + 32-bit value -> actor hex + 64-bit counter) and the version-vector encoding (dense array indexed by replica id -> sparse object keyed by actor hex) both changed. No migration path, deliberately: there is no production data, and a compatibility shim for a field that was never an identity would be worse than the cut.

collabedit's loadOrAssignReplicaId() -- which drew a random 16-bit id, scanned peers' presence.json for taken values and wrote the winner to a text file -- is replaced by ReplicaState::open(), which mints 128 bits once and persists them before any operation exists. This was app code, but it was identity plumbing rather than a widget feature, and leaving a 16-bit draw feeding a 128-bit engine was not an option.

Seed operations no longer use replica 0. seed_actor() derives the actor from the content (domain-separated SHA-256), because replica 0 was also the default replica of every engine that did not configure one, and two peers seeding different content into one document both claimed replica 0's counter range.

remaining_scope: Step 3b (still in this task): run-interval allocation. Replace the per-scalar tick in apply_validated_local_edit and IdList's insert/remove with one checked reserve_run(n + 1) borrowed from a durable allocator, so an operation's identity is base + n -- strictly above every item it created and strictly below the next operation's base. This is the change that removes today's aliasing (op.timestamp == the last item identity of its own run) and the second deletion_ts tick. Sections 3.2-3.7 are written and modelled; nothing enforces them against Buffer/IdList yet.

Step 3c: the engine must BORROW its allocator, never own one. A Buffer constructed with an ActorId does not create a counter and is not authority to restart one (section 3.7); the counter lives in ReplicaState. Tests that want a throwaway counter must say so explicitly as a volatile test counter -- never by reusing a production allocator path.

Step 5: reject a default-constructed ActorId at the public boundary. check_counter() now refuses counter 0 and an all-zero actor inside validate_operation_identity, so the engine already refuses such an operation; what remains is refusing to CONSTRUCT one. CrdtEngine and CollabDocument no longer have a defaulted replica argument, and tst_operation_validation covers the operation case; add the construction case and state it in the public API guide.

Step 6: opaque operation values -- move EditOperation/UndoOperation field layout out of the public header so the fast paths reach fields through internal accessors. Do this after 3b, since both touch Operations.h.

Inherited obligations this step created for other tasks: P06b must carry each operation's interval length and the gap-record kind, and the versioned sparse codec replaces the interim JSON identity/version-vector encodings written here. P07 must refuse a mismatched interval and a gap that is not terminal. L02 owns gap-record publication and the reopen path. L04 owns the stream envelope: StreamEntry::replica_id, ChatMessage::replica_id and Comment::replica_id are still 16-bit producer ids and are NOT this device's actor (collabedit now writes 0 rather than a number that means nothing), and the ack-frontier file key is still a decimal replica id. The decided *structure* of acks.json (sibling per replica, keyed by peer, min over peers) is unchanged; only the key's spelling follows the identity.
Left deliberately alone: SegmentFormat's first_lamport/last_lamport u64 header fields keep their names. They are counters, and segment framing belongs to L02.
